function.name: get_account_transactions
function.description: Fetch parameterized read-only transaction history for a specific account within `days_back`.

function.name: find_candidate_fund_flows
function.description: Run deterministic MultiDiGraph fund-flow path reconstruction with exact Decimal math.

parameters.description: Graph flow search input; `transactions` defaults to all transactions already loaded in state.

transactions.description: Optional explicit transaction list; omit to analyze all transactions fetched in this session.

function.name: compute_flow_conservation
function.description: Compute exact Decimal inflow/outflow conservation and structuring flags across candidate paths.

parameters.description: Decimal flow conservation check over reconstructed candidate paths.

path_ids.description: Path IDs (e.g. ['PATH-1']) to verify; omit/empty to check top reconstructed multi-hop paths.

function.name: compare_graph_runs
function.description: Compare the previous and latest graph runs to identify newly discovered paths.

parameters.description: Compare the two most recent graph scans to inspect newly uncovered consolidation paths.

note.description: Optional note explaining what delta is being checked

function.name: calc
function.description: Exact Decimal calculator (`sum`, `diff`, `pct`, `compare`); registers a `CALC-*` evidence entry.

parameters.description: Exact Decimal calculator (`sum`, `diff`, `pct`, `compare`) so the LLM never computes mental math.

op.description: Operation: 'sum' (sum all values), 'diff' (a - b), 'pct' ((a / b) * 100), 'compare' (a vs b).

values.description: Exact numeric strings from tool outputs (e.g. ['900000.00', '828000.00']); 2 items for diff/pct.

label.description: Short description of what figure is being computed

note.description: Optional note explaining what delta is being checked

function.name: calc
function.description: Exact Decimal calculator (`sum`, `diff`, `pct`, `compare`); registers a `CALC-*` evidence entry.

parameters.description: Exact Decimal calculator (`sum`, `diff`, `pct`, `compare`) so the LLM never computes mental math.

op.description: Operation: 'sum' (sum all values), 'diff' (a - b), 'pct' ((a / b) * 100), 'compare' (a vs b).

values.description: Exact numeric strings from tool outputs (e.g. ['900000.00', '828000.00']); 2 items for diff/pct.

label.description: Short description of what figure is being computed

You are C2 Specialist `regulatory_analyst` operating under Indian PMLA / RBI / FIU-IND rules.
Assigned Objective: Regulatory lookup and citation: 1) search applicable AML/KYC regulations for the relevant jurisdictions implied by the root/counterparty profiles and the INR transaction amount, 2) extract clause text for reporting thresholds, suspicious transaction definitions (especially scatter/gather typologies), and required escalation procedures. Deliverables: list of applicable regulations and exact clause excerpts to support escalation recommendations.
Maximum Tool Calls Allowed in This Hand-Off: 2
STRICT CONSTRAINTS:
- Invoke ONLY tools provided in your function schema.

- Never compute mental INR math; use `calc` or copy exact tool figures.

messages.content: {"abstain_reason": "", "abstained": false, "clauses": [{"category": "str_obligation", "clause_id": "PMLA-2002-S12-P02", "effective_date": "2013-02-15", "human_verified": false, "relevance_score": 1.0, "retrieval_date": "2026-11-24", "source": "Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002", "source_type": "regulatory", "source_url": "https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/[ACCOUNT_NUMBER:12***89]/2036", "text": "<untrusted_data source=\"PMLA-2002-S12-P02.text\">Under Section 12(1)(b) of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, every reporting entity is legally obligated to furnish to the Director of the Financial Intelligence Unit - India (FIU-IND), within such time as may be prescribed under the Maintenance of Records Rules, information relating to prescribed transactions, whether attempted or executed, the nature and value of which may be prescribed. This statutory duty encompasses Cash Transaction Reports, Cross-Border Wire Transfer Reports, Counterfeit Currency Reports, Non-Profit Organisation Transaction Reports, and Suspicious Transaction Reports. Attempted suspicious transactions that are aborted or partially blocked before settlement still require full documentation and assessment for statutory reporting under Section 12(1)(b).</untrusted_data>", "title": "Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 (Section 12(1)(b))"}, {"category": "confidentiality", "clause_id": "PMLA-2002-S12-P04", "effective_date": "2013-02-15", "human_verified": false, "relevance_score": 0.9535, "retrieval_date": "2026-11-24", "source": "Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002", "source_type": "regulatory", "source_url": "https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/[ACCOUNT_NUMBER:12***89]/2036", "text": "<untrusted_data source=\"PMLA-2002-S12-P04.text\">Section 12(2) of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 mandates that every information maintained, furnished, or verified\u2014save as otherwise provided under any law for the time being in force\u2014shall be kept confidential. Reporting entities, compliance analysts, and technology systems supporting AML alert triage must safeguard investigation worksheets, STR drafts, escalation rationales, and FIU-IND correspondence against unauthorized disclosure. In particular, customers under active alert investigation must never be alerted or tipped off that their transactions are undergoing suspicious activity scrutiny or that a Suspicious Transaction Report is being prepared for submission to the Director, FIU-IND, as disclosure compromises statutory intelligence gathering.</untrusted_data>", "title": "Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 (Section 12(2) (Confidentiality))"}, {"category": "str_standard", "clause_id": "PMLA-2002-S3-P06", "effective_date": "2005-07-01", "human_verified": false, "relevance_score": 0.9489, "retrieval_date": "2026-11-24", "source": "Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002", "source_type": "regulatory", "source_url": "https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/[ACCOUNT_NUMBER:12***89]/2036", "text": "<untrusted_data source=\"PMLA-2002-S3-P06.text\">Although criminal prosecution under Section 3 of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 ultimately depends on proceeds connected to a scheduled offence listed in the Schedule to the Act, reporting entities and bank compliance investigators are neither equipped nor expected to prove a predicate crime before escalating a Suspicious Transaction Report.   Excerpt:
  "<untrusted_data source=\"PMLA-2002-S12-P02.text\">Under Section 12(1)(b) of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, every reporting entity is legally obligated to furnish to the Director of the Financial Intelligence Unit - India (FIU-IND), within such time as may be prescribed under the Maintenance of Records Rules, information relating to prescribed transactions, whether attempted or executed, the nature and value of which may be prescribed. This statutory duty encompasses Cash Transaction Reports, Cross-Border Wire Transfer Reports, Counterfeit Currency Reports, Non-Profit Organisation Transaction Reports, and Suspicious Transaction Reports. Attempted suspicious transactions that are aborted or partially blocked before settlement still require full documentation and assessment for statutory reporting under Section 12(1)(b).</untrusted_data>"

The Principal Officer of a reporting entity shall furnish the information referred to in clause (D) of sub-rule (1) of Rule 3 promptly in writing, or by fax or electronic mail, to the Director, FIU-IND not later than seven working days on being satisfied that the transaction is suspicious. The seven working-day clock begins upon the Principal Officer's satisfaction of reasonable grounds of suspicion following investigation, making timely alert triage, bounded replanning, and clear evidentiary packaging essential for statutory compliance.</untrusted_data>"

  Excerpt:

In scatter-gather alert reviews, demonstrating the absence of economic rationale requires examining both suspicious topology (dispersion, intermediary skimming, rapid or staggered reconsolidation) and benign commercial hypotheses (registered marketplace escrow, corporate payroll, licensed chit pools, or verifiable charity relief) before concluding whether reasonable grounds of suspicion exist.</untrusted_data>"

Banks must examine as far as possible the background and purpose of such transactions and record their findings in writing for at least five years. response.text:
Hand-off HO-REG (ALT-V2-D0007) — regulatory retrieval summary and next steps

Case snapshot (from context)
- Alert ID: ALT-V2-D0007
- Root account: ACC-D0007-RT00
- Network accounts: ACC-D0007-IN01..IN04, ACC-D0007-DS01..DS04
- Path nodes and flow_finding: multi-hop path reconstruction present; flow_tracer completed (35 evidence items)

Regulatory / SOP passages retrieved (cite only IDs)
- SOP-SG-008 (AuditGuard — case-specific query requirement)
- PMLR-2005-R9-P10 (PML Rules 2005 — Rule 9: periodic KYC refresh / expired credentials)
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-10 (FIU-IND Banking indicator — circular / round-trip transfers)
- SOP-SG-004 (AuditGuard — payroll verification criteria)
- SOP-SG-002 (AuditGuard — external-bank & missing evidence protocol)
- PMLA-2002-S3-P05 (PMLA 2002 — Section 3: placement/layering typologies)
- SOP-SG-003 (AuditGuard — benign look-alikes corroboration)
- SOP-SG-010 (AuditGuard — degraded tool / fail-closed escalation)
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-11 (FIU-IND Banking indicator — business flows via personal accounts)
- RBI-KYC-2016-P64-P03 (RBI KYC Master Direction Para 64 — originator/beneficiary info & missing-leg obligations)

Key regulatory takeaways (concise)
- Require case-specific corroboration and explicit missing-evidence disclosure before disposition (SOP-SG-008). 
- Accounts in the network with expired/missing KYC or missing PAN must be flagged and require fresh CDD before benign closure (PMLR-2005-R9-P10). 
- Round-trip / circular scatter-gather patterns that reconstruct cycles or near-exact conservation across hops are red flags and support escalation for STR review if benign hypotheses cannot be independently corroborated (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-10; PMLA-2002-S3-P05). 
- Verify whether the pattern aligns with legitimate payroll or marketplace escrow flows; payroll closures require the four corroborating checks (SOP-SG-004; SOP-SG-003). 
- If any transfer legs exit to external banks, or internal tools return degraded responses, enumerate missing items and treat disposition as request_info rather than close_benign (SOP-SG-002; SOP-SG-010; RBI-KYC-2016-P64-P03). 
- Use FIU indicator on use of personal accounts for business flows—if high-frequency settlement is via savings accounts, demand statutory registry corroboration (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-11).

Observed investigation gaps to include in the HO
(List these explicitly in the hand-off worksheet under missing_evidence — per SOP-SG-002 / SOP-SG-010)
1. KYC files: fresh OVD and PAN verification status for ACC-D0007-IN01..IN04 and ACC-D0007-DS01..DS04 (PMLR-2005-R9-P10).
2. Inter-bank wire metadata for any legs that flow to/from external correspondent banks (RBI-KYC-2016-P64-P03; SOP-SG-002).
3. Full flow_tracer metadata and chain-of-custody for the 35 evidence items (document any truncated or degraded entries) (SOP-SG-010).
4. Commercial registry proof (MCA/GST/EPFO) or vendor/employee roster documentation if a payroll/escrow hypothesis is asserted (SOP-SG-004; SOP-SG-003; FIU-IND-RFI-BA-11).
5. Precise amounts/decimal conservation checks across multi-hop dispersals and reconsolidations to test round-trip conservation (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-10; PMLA-2002-S3-P05).

Recommended immediate actions (regulatory-aligned)
- Mark disposition as request_info (fail-closed) until missing items (1–4 above) are collected — per SOP-SG-002, SOP-SG-010, RBI-KYC-2016-P64-P03.
- Request from operations / payments team:
  - Complete KYC packs + PAN for each network account.
  - Inter-bank SWIFT/NEFT/RTGS metadata for all external legs in the lookback window.
  - Untampered flow_tracer logs and the 35 evidence item artifacts for integrity verification.
- Parallel verification tasks for benign hypotheses:
  - Check commercial registries (MCA / GST / EPFO) for any root or network accounts (SOP-SG-004; SOP-SG-003).
  - Pull counterparty payment cadence history for network accounts to confirm or refute payroll/escrow cadence (SOP-SG-003).
- If, after obtaining the requested evidence, the pattern still shows circular round-trip conservation or lack of commercial corroboration, prepare STR referral package referencing FIU-IND indicators and PMLA Section 3 guidance (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-10; PMLA-2002-S3-P05).

Required documentation for hand-off to Principal Officer / Compliance
- This summary plus an attached missing_evidence list (items 1–4), copies of all retrieved flow_tracer evidence (with integrity/hash if available), and a log of any degraded tool errors (per SOP-SG-010).
- Cite the following clause IDs in the worksheet as the basis for requesting information and fail-closed handling: SOP-SG-008; SOP-SG-002; SOP-SG-010; PMLR-2005-R9-P10; RBI-KYC-2016-P64-P03; FIU-IND-RFI-BA-10; PMLA-2002-S3-P05; SOP-SG-004; SOP-SG-003; FIU-IND-RFI-BA-11.

Tool usage note
- Retrieval executed using case-specific queries per SOP-SG-008. Clause IDs above are the exact passages returned by the regulatory retrieval tool and must be cited in the HO worksheet.

If you want, I can:
- Draft the missing_evidence checklist in the required HO worksheet format (including fields for request owner, deadline, and required artifact hashes), or
- Prepare a template STR-scoping memo (if evidence persists supporting escalation) that cites the specific clause IDs above.

response.text:
Summary (case ALT-V2-D0008 — observed flow amount INR 4,480,723.63)

Relevant regulatory passages (IDs returned from repository search)
- PMLA-2002-S12-P02 — Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, Section 12(1)(b): obligation to furnish prescribed transaction information to FIU-IND (CTR, STR, CBWTR, etc.), including attempted/aborted suspicious transactions.
- PMLA-2002-S12A-P01 — Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, Section 12A(1): FIU-IND power to call records; keep complete supporting audit trail.
- PMLA-2002-S12A-P02 — Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, Section 12A(2)-(3): confidentiality of FIU requests and five-year record retention obligations.
- PMLA-2002-S12AA-P02 — Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, Section 12AA(1)(c) & (2): Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) obligations and refusal of transaction where EDD not satisfied.
- PMLA-2002-S12AA-P03 — Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, Section 12AA(3)-(4): increased monitoring after suspicious transactions and 5-year retention of EDD evidence.
- PMLR-2005-R3-P05 — Prevention of Money-Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005, Rule 3(1)(B): aggregate integrally connected cash transactions; threshold aggregation rules for INR 10,00,000 CTR trigger and structuring indicators.
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-03 — FIU-IND Banking Red Flag: structuring/smurfing below INR 10,00,000 (fragmentation patterns; aggregate across rolling windows).
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-01 — FIU-IND Banking Red Flag: rapid pass-through / scatter–gather layering (immediate dispersion and subsequent reconsolidation within 7–30 days).
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-06 — FIU-IND Banking Red Flag: sudden high-value activity in newly opened or dormant accounts (mule/TAKOVER pattern).
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-16 — FIU-IND Banking Red Flag: PEP-linked complex transfers; requirement for EDD and senior approval.

Key regulatory points extracted (paraphrased from the cited clauses)
- Reporting duty: Reporting entities must report prescribed transactions and suspicious transactions to FIU-IND and keep complete records for regulatory calls (PMLA-2002-S12-P02; PMLA-2002-S12A-P01; PMLA-2002-S12A-P02).
- CTR/aggregation threshold: Cash transactions integrally connected must be aggregated; when monthly aggregate crosses INR 10,00,000, CTR/aggregation rules apply and deliberate fragmentation is a red flag (PMLR-2005-R3-P05; FIU-IND-RFI-BA-03).
- Scatter/gather & layering: Rapid pass-through where credits are dispersed across many intermediaries and reconsolidate within 7–30 days is a strong layering indicator (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-01).
- Dormant/new account exploitation: Newly reactivated or recently opened low-history accounts with sudden high-value in/out flows that return to near-zero balance are flagged as mule accounts/TAKOVER (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-06).
- EDD & escalation: Where transactions are suspicious, EDD must be applied; if EDD conditions are not met, transactional activity should be blocked/refused and further monitoring and STR filing taken (PMLA-2002-S12AA-P02; PMLA-2002-S12AA-P03).
- PEPs: Transactions involving PEPs or their associates require elevated suspicion, senior approval, and enhanced monitoring (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-16).

Replan run added CALC-0472AB416F01 and PATH evidence (PATH-6ECEDBB34E4E, PATH-3CF39614199E, PATH-C0A06439C7D8) showing total_outflow_inr='2184809.72' per path and high retention_pct (99.29 / 96.48 / 96.80). Aggregated sum of the three reported path outflows is '6554429.16' (CALC-9835BEBD). Given KYC indicates the root (KYC-ACC-D0005-RT00) is a registered employer with declared_annual_income_inr='7489935.71' but counterparties include unregistered entities (KYC-ACC-D0005-IN01, KYC-ACC-D0005-IN02) and unexplained large net_differences (e.g. PATH-6ECEDBB34E4E net_difference_inr='2169372.95'), further information is required to close the case reliably. suspicious_hypothesis.explanation: The observed multi-hop paths show very high retention_pct (fee-skimming pattern) where >96% of total_outflow_inr is not consolidated back into downstream accounts, producing large net differences inconsistent with routine business passthrough. Aggregation of the three reported path outflows equals '6554429.16' (CALC-9835BEBD), while individual path net differences are substantial (e.g. PATH-6ECEDBB34E4E net_difference_inr='2169372.95'). Some counterparties lack commercial registration and have medium/low KYC confidence. This pattern is consistent with potential evasive layering or unauthorized diversion of funds and warrants further FIU reporting and deeper counterparty verification.

benign_hypothesis.explanation: The root account (KYC-ACC-D0005-RT00) is a registered employer with declared_annual_income_inr='7489935.71' and documented seasonal volume spikes. The observed high retention_pct across paths may reflect legitimate operational fees, split settlements, or timing mismatches across settlement cycles rather than illicit diversion. Some counterparties (e.g. ACC-D0005-IN02) have standard KYC and PAN verification.

function.name: find_candidate_fund_flows
function.description: Run deterministic MultiDiGraph fund-flow path reconstruction with exact Decimal math.

parameters.description: Graph flow search input; `transactions` defaults to all transactions already loaded in state.

transactions.description: Optional explicit transaction list; omit to analyze all transactions fetched in this session.

function.name: compute_flow_conservation
function.description: Compute exact Decimal inflow/outflow conservation and structuring flags across candidate paths.

parameters.description: Decimal flow conservation check over reconstructed candidate paths.

path_ids.description: Path IDs (e.g. ['PATH-1']) to verify; omit/empty to check top reconstructed multi-hop paths.

function.name: compare_graph_runs
function.description: Compare the previous and latest graph runs to identify newly discovered paths.

parameters.description: Compare the two most recent graph scans to inspect newly uncovered consolidation paths.

note.description: Optional note explaining what delta is being checked

function.name: calc
function.description: Exact Decimal calculator (`sum`, `diff`, `pct`, `compare`); registers a `CALC-*` evidence entry.

parameters.description: Exact Decimal calculator (`sum`, `diff`, `pct`, `compare`) so the LLM never computes mental math.

op.description: Operation: 'sum' (sum all values), 'diff' (a - b), 'pct' ((a / b) * 100), 'compare' (a vs b).

values.description: Exact numeric strings from tool outputs (e.g. ['900000.00', '828000.00']); 2 items for diff/pct.

label.description: Short description of what figure is being computed

function.name: finish
function.description: Complete the investigation and submit a structured worksheet with both hypotheses and missing evidence.

parameters.description: Terminal tool submitting the structured `DispositionWorksheet` draft for deterministic verification.

recommendation_rationale.description: Concise rationale citing exact tool IDs and copying INR figures verbatim from tool outputs.

suspicious_hypothesis.description: Structured hypothesis entry required for both `suspicious` and `benign` perspectives.

regulatory_citations.description: Retrieved passage IDs (e.g. PMLA-2002-*, PMLR-2005-*, RBI-KYC-2016-*, FIU-IND-RFI-*, FATF-*, SOP-*)

benign_hypothesis.description: Structured hypothesis entry required for both `suspicious` and `benign` perspectives.

regulatory_citations.description: Retrieved passage IDs (e.g. PMLA-2002-*, PMLR-2005-*, RBI-KYC-2016-*, FIU-IND-RFI-*, FATF-*, SOP-*)

missing_evidence.description: Explicit list of missing or out-of-band evidence items (required on every case).

regulatory_citations.description: Verified regulatory clause IDs retrieved from `compliance-kb`.

tool_calls.name: finish

function.name: find_candidate_fund_flows
function.description: Run deterministic MultiDiGraph fund-flow path reconstruction with exact Decimal math.

parameters.description: Graph flow search input; `transactions` defaults to all transactions already loaded in state.

transactions.description: Optional explicit transaction list; omit to analyze all transactions fetched in this session.

function.description: Compute exact Decimal inflow/outflow conservation and structuring flags across candidate paths.

parameters.description: Decimal flow conservation check over reconstructed candidate paths.

path_ids.description: Path IDs (e.g. ['PATH-1']) to verify; omit/empty to check top reconstructed multi-hop paths.

function.name: compare_graph_runs
function.description: Compare the previous and latest graph runs to identify newly discovered paths.

parameters.description: Compare the two most recent graph scans to inspect newly uncovered consolidation paths.

note.description: Optional note explaining what delta is being checked

function.name: calc
function.description: Exact Decimal calculator (`sum`, `diff`, `pct`, `compare`); registers a `CALC-*` evidence entry.

parameters.description: Exact Decimal calculator (`sum`, `diff`, `pct`, `compare`) so the LLM never computes mental math.

op.description: Operation: 'sum' (sum all values), 'diff' (a - b), 'pct' ((a / b) * 100), 'compare' (a vs b).

values.description: Exact numeric strings from tool outputs (e.g. ['900000.00', '828000.00']); 2 items for diff/pct.

label.description: Short description of what figure is being computed

Summary judgment (recommended escalation): escalate for Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to FIU-IND and perform Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) now.

Why: the observed scatter–gather / rapid pass‑through pattern across the listed network accounts, with a consolidated value of INR 5,428,457.33, matches FIU‑IND red flags for layering/rapid pass‑through and structuring/threshold evasion and meets statutory reporting obligations under PMLA. The pattern requires written documentation, aggregation across linked legs, source‑of‑funds verification and STR filing rather than non‑action.

Key regulatory passages (exact IDs and short justifications)
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-01 — FIU‑IND Banking Red Flag: rapid pass‑through / scatter‑gather reconsolidation into single beneficiary within 7–30 days; requires STR scrutiny and reconstruction of multi‑hop paths.
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-03 — FIU‑IND Banking Red Flag: structuring (smurfing) — aggregation across rolling monthly windows; fragmentation below INR 10,00,000 is itself a red flag requiring STR evaluation.
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-17 — FIU‑IND Banking Red Flag: split IMPS/NEFT velocity spikes and immediate onward movement; compare to 90‑day baseline to distinguish commercial spikes from coordinated structuring.
- RBI-KYC-2016-P35-P02 — RBI KYC Master Direction: pay special attention to complex/unusually large transactions and multi‑hop scatter‑gather loops; reconstruct paths, check decimal conservation, verify intermediary commercial registration or recurring counterparty history; record findings in writing for at least five years.
- PMLR-2005-R3-P05 (Rule 3(1)(B)) — PML Rules: aggregate integrally connected cash/electronic transactions across rolling monthly windows when individual legs are split to evade the INR 10,00,000 CTR threshold; Rule 3 triggers STR scrutiny for deliberate evasion.
- PMLA-2002-S12-P02 (Section 12(1)(b)) — PMLA: reporting entities must furnish prescribed transaction information to FIU‑IND (including STRs); attempted/aborted suspicious transactions still require assessment and reporting.
- RBI-KYC-2016-P13-P01 — RBI KYC Master Direction Para 13: CDD/EDD triggers include occasional transactions beyond specified amounts, and whenever there is suspicion of money‑laundering regardless of thresholds; EDD must verify source of funds/wealth and beneficial ownership.
- RBI-KYC-2016-P70-P02 & RBI-KYC-2016-P70-P01 — RBI KYC Master Direction Para 70: STR filing is an intelligence obligation (not a finding of guilt); do not tip off customers; avoid account restrictions solely because an STR was filed; maintain confidentiality.
- PMLA-2002-S12-P04 — PMLA Section 12(2): confidentiality/tipping‑off prohibition; keep STR deliberations and correspondence confidential.

Operational steps to take now (concise)
1. Immediate analyst actions (non‑tipping off):
   - Prepare STR draft with timeline, linked account IDs (include ACC-D0009-RT00 and listed network accounts), transaction amounts, timestamps, counterparty details and exact decimal sums linking dispersed outflows and consolidated inflows.
   - Preserve and copy all electronic/messaging/transaction logs and counterparty KYC files into a secured investigation folder (access‑restricted).
   - Do not freeze or close accounts solely because of STR filing; apply risk‑based enhanced monitoring pending further instructions (RBI-KYC-2016-P70-P02).

2. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) required (RBI-KYC-2016-P13-P01):
   - Verify beneficial ownership for each intermediary account, obtain underlying commercial registrations/GST invoices or payroll/contract documents where claimed.
   - Obtain source of funds / source of wealth documentation for originator(s) and final beneficiary.
   - Reconstruct multi‑hop flows across the investigation lookback window (7–30 days per FIU indicator) and check exact decimal conservation (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-01; RBI-KYC-2016-P35-P02).

3. Aggregation and threshold tests (PMLR-2005-R3-P05; FIU-IND-RFI-BA-03):
   - Aggregate related cash/electronic legs across rolling monthly windows to test for deliberate fragmentation below INR 10,00,000.
   - If monthly aggregated linked value exceeds CTR thresholds or shows deliberate structuring, include that evidence in STR.

4. Prepare documentation and retention:
   - Record all findings, rationales, EDD results and escalation decisions in writing and retain for at least five years (RBI-KYC-2016-P35-P02).
   - Maintain strict confidentiality controls (RBI-KYC-2016-P70-P01; PMLA-2002-S12-P04).

Missing / degraded evidence to obtain urgently
- Source of funds documentation for the originator(s) and justification for why funds were split across the network accounts.
- Proof of commercial purpose (invoices, contracts, GST returns) for each intermediary if entities claim business reasons.
- Beneficial ownership details for intermediary accounts (UBOs, ownership chain).
- Precise time stamps and transaction reference IDs to verify decimal conservation between dispersed and reconsolidated legs.
- Any prior recurring transaction history to establish whether current pattern is an anomaly vs. legitimate seasonal/commercial activity.

Decision rationale (concise)
- The consolidated amount (INR 5,428,457.33) is materially large and, given the scatter–gather pattern across multiple unrelated accounts, matches FIU‑IND layering and structuring indicators that mandate STR scrutiny (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-01, FIU-IND-RFI-BA-03).
- PMLA and PML Rules require reporting of suspicious/structuring activity and aggregation across linked legs (PMLA-2002-S12-P02; PMLR-2005-R3-P05).
- RBI KYC guidance requires EDD and written findings, and prohibits tipping off (RBI-KYC-2016-P35-P02; RBI-KYC-2016-P13-P01; RBI-KYC-2016-P70-P01/P02

response.text:
Summary of applicable statutes / clauses (exact IDs cited), thresholds, timelines, and recommended actions for the observed "scatter–gather" INR transfer pattern (alert ALT-V2-D0010):

1) Key regulatory passages and what they require (IDs)
- PMLR-2005-R3-P05 — Rule 3(1)(B): treat integrally connected cash (and coordinated deposits) split below INR 10,00,000 as aggregated for CTR purposes and as structuring/smurfing indicators.  
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-03 — FIU-IND Banking Red Flag (Structuring): repeated transfers just below INR 10,00,000 or coordinated multi-account fragmentation require aggregation and STR consideration.  
- PMLR-2005-R3-P03 — Rule 3(1)(C)-(D): suspicious transactions (cash or non-cash, incl. electronic transfers) must be recorded and assessed for STR filing regardless of amount.  
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-17 — FIU-IND Banking Red Flag (Split IMPS/NEFT bursts): bursts of small electronic legs with immediate onward movement are red flags and should be aggregated across windows.  
- FIU-IND-RFI-BA-20 — FIU-IND Banking Red Flag (Customer evasiveness): inability to provide coherent economic purpose or KYC/documentary backing strengthens reasonable suspicion.  
- FATF-R20-P02 — FATF Rec.20 interpretive note: suspicious transactions (including attempted/split/low-value) must be reported irrespective of amount.  
- PMLR-2005-R8-P01 — Rule 8(1): filing timetable — periodic CTR/CBWTR by 15th of succeeding month; STRs to be filed promptly and not later than seven working days after Principal Officer is satisfied of reasonable grounds. (Full text retrieved: PMLR-2005-R8-P01)  
- RBI-KYC-2016-P70-P01 / P70-P02 — RBI KYC Master Direction Para 70: strict anti-tipping-off/confidentiality when filing STRs; do not restrain accounts solely because an STR is filed — apply risk-based enhanced monitoring and await lawful directions.

2) Thresholds, timelines and filing triggers (from cited passages)
- Cash Transaction Report (CTR) threshold: INR 10,00,000 (Rule 3(1)(A)/(B) references; FIU indicator references). (See PMLR-2005-R3-P05, FIU-IND-RFI-BA-03.)  
- Cross-border wire transfer reporting threshold cited: INR 5,00,000 for CBWTR (see PMLR-2005-R8-P01).  
- STR filing: no monetary minimum — report suspicious transactions regardless of value (FATF-R20-P02; PMLR-2005-R3-P03; FIU indicators).  
- Filing timelines: periodic threshold reports (CTR/CBWTR/NTR) — by 15th day of succeeding month; STRs — promptly and not later than seven working days after Principal Officer is satisfied of reasonable grounds (PMLR-2005-R8-P01).

3) How these apply to the observed pattern (mapping from facts to obligations)
- Pattern: scatter–gather / pass-through INR transfers across network accounts (ACC-D0010-RT00, ACC-D0010-IN01/02/03, ACC-D0010-DS01), multiple legs and 44 evidence items recorded by flow_tracer.  
- Apply aggregation rules: if multiple legs (cash or electronic) are integrally connected or coordinated to evade thresholds, aggregate across a rolling monthly window to determine whether CTR threshold (INR 10,00,000) or CBWTR thresholds are breached (PMLR-2005-R3-P05; FIU-IND-RFI-BA-03; FIU-IND-RFI-BA-17).  
- Independent STR trigger: even if individual legs remain below statutory monetary thresholds, the pattern (structured fragmentation, rapid onward forwarding, lack of commercial documentation or evasive responses) gives reasonable grounds for suspicion and requires STR assessment and likely filing (PMLR-2005-R3-P03; FIU-IND-RFI-BA-20; FATF-R20-P02).

4) Recommended compliance actions (operational steps tied to the facts)
- Immediately aggregate all related INR legs across the rolling monthly window for ACC-D0010-RT00 and the listed network accounts to test against CTR/CBWTR thresholds (use exact decimal sums). Cite and preserve the aggregation workpapers. (PMLR-2005-R3-P05; FIU-IND-RFI-BA-03.)  
- Conduct enhanced due diligence (call-down KYC, request invoices/GST, beneficial owner verification) framed neutrally as standard KYC requests (avoid tipping-off). Document responses, gaps, and evasiveness. (FIU-IND-RFI-BA-20; RBI-KYC-2016-P70-P01.)  
- If aggregation shows threshold breaches: ensure periodic CTR/CBWTR filings by the 15th of the succeeding month and preserve records per Rule 3. (PMLR-2005-R8-P01.)  
- If reasonable grounds of suspicion exist (structuring, burst transfers, lack of economic rationale, evasive customer responses or rapid onward movement): Principal Officer should approve an STR and file promptly and in any event within seven working days of satisfaction of suspicion. Preserve all logs/evidence and avoid tipping-off. (PMLR-2005-R3-P03; PMLR-2005-R8-P01; FATF-R20-P02; RBI-KYC-2016-P70-P01.)  
- Apply risk-based enhanced monitoring (transaction blocks or restrictions only if legally required or after receiving lawful direction). Do not publicly disclose the STR or suggest that reporting is occurring. (RBI-KYC-2016-P70-P02.)

5) Required preservation & confidentiality
- Retain full records of aggregation logic, transaction chains, KYC requests/responses, and communication logs as required under PMLR record-keeping and FIU guidance
